criteria.criterion: A free-function gh::land_pr test with a fake host reads the records branch and finds a landing-intent record then a landing record, in that order. Intent: PR number, head sha, head tree, expected base, job ids. Landing: PR number, head sha, host commit, merge method, commits with tree/job/verification, intent id. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: land_pr_writes_the_intent_then_the_landing_with_the_head_as_second_parent (gh.rs:3634) reads the bare remote's athena/records in first-parent order. It asserts records[0] is a LandingIntent and records[1] is a Landing. Intent: pr_number 42, head_sha, head_tree_sha, expected_base == remote trunk tip, job_ids. Landing: pr_number, head_sha, host_commit, merge_method Merge, intent id, and commits [{sha, tree, job, verification}]. It also calls validate() on both. Passed.

criteria.criterion: A test shows the records commit carrying the landing record has the PR head sha as its second parent. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: The same test asserts bare.parents(landing_commit) == [intent_commit, world.head] and that the intent commit has no parents. In athena-git, a_remote_append_publishes_first_then_moves_the_local_branch_and_keeps_extra_parents asserts parents == [first, work]. Both passed.

criteria.criterion: A test with a fake host that refuses the merge shows the local and remote records branch hold the intent and no landing record, and land_pr returns its existing error. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: a_refused_merge_leaves_the_intent_on_both_branches_and_no_landing: the error contains 'the host refused the merge', and the remote has 1 intent and 0 landings. The local RECORDS_REF equals the remote tip. Passed.

criteria.criterion: A call-order test with a bare remote shows the intent is on the remote before PrHost::merge is called and the landing record after. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: the_intent_is_on_the_remote_before_the_merge_and_the_landing_after: the fake host's on_merge hook reads the bare remote at merge time and sees (1 intent, 0 landings). After land_pr returns, the remote holds 1 intent and 1 landing. Passed.

criteria.criterion: Rejected-push test: the remote records branch moves between build and push; the commit is rebuilt on the fetched remote tip and retried (bounded), succeeds, and local and remote tips match; the local ref moves only after a successful push. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: a_rejected_push_is_rebuilt_on_the_fetched_remote_tip_and_retried: a rival clone pushes inside the before_push hook. Both passed.

criteria.criterion: Leftover-local-intent test: a local records ref ahead of or diverged from the remote is reset to the remote before writing; the next land_pr succeeds with no divergence error. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: a_leftover_local_records_branch_is_reset_to_the_remote_before_writing (gh.rs:3776): a local-only commit sits on top of the intent, and another clone moves the remote, so the branches have diverged. The athena-git test sync_from_resets_a_local_branch_that_is_ahead_or_diverged_and_the_next_write_succeeds covers both the ahead and the diverged case. Both passed.

summary: The candidate does what the reading asks. When the merge gate is open, gh::land_pr now writes a validated LandingIntent to origin's athena/records before it calls PrHost::merge. Once the merge is confirmed, it writes a Landing whose records commit has the PR head as its second parent. Both go through the existing RecordsWriter, which gains two methods. append_to_remote builds on the remote tip, pushes with an expected-tip guard, moves the local ref only after a successful push, and retries at most 8 times before returning Contended. sync_from resets the local records branch to the remote. Athena::land_pr builds the sink with GitLandingRecords::for_remote and passes it on, with no None fallback, and drain.rs reaches it through Athena::land_pr. I ran the 8 new athena-core records_flow tests, the 12 athena-git records_branch tests and the new Git test; all passed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full-test checks passed on this tree. The design doc has the sync_from explanation and a failure-path table, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry. drain.rs and athena-core/Cargo.toml were planned but did not change, and neither needed to. The only gaps are minor: the new warning line in display.rs has no test, and my judgement that the tests fail without the change comes from reading them; I did not run them against the base code.
